newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Safrica demands regional commander for Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Safrica demands regional commander for Zaire force.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Tuesday South Africa would contribute troops to a multinational peace force for Zaire only if they were led by an officer from the region.
"I am not prepared to put my troops under any other commander except a commander from the Great Lakes," Mandela told reporters.
"I don't want a commander even from the SADC (Southern African Development Community) region. I want a commander from the Great Lakes because they know that area very well," Mandela said.
South Africa has expressed willingness to contribute to a peace force for Zaire but has not said what form its help would take. Canada has been given the leading role in the force.
Mandela said he discussed the issue on Monday night with former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere, who is playing a leading mediation role.
"I spoke to the former president Nyerere last night and he indicated to us what we should do and we will follow that," Mandela said without elaborating.
The peace force mission has become unclear as thousands of Hutu refugees flock home peacefully, quitting the war zone in the Goma area of rebel-held eastern Zaire.
Many countries, such as the United States and Britain, were reluctant participants and have seized on the mass migration as a sign the force should be radically reduced in size or even scrapped.
